status: published with v0.8, 2026-11-02 — independently re-derived 2026-10-30 (see README)
what_this_proves: That two parties who provisioned the same profile through different channels compute the same profile_hash. The hash is over the RFC 8785 (JCS) serialization of the PARSED profile document, never over file bytes — formatting, key order, and trailing newlines do not change it.
rules: Parse the profile JSON, serialize with RFC 8785 JCS (UTF-8, sorted keys, no whitespace, shortest numbers), sha256 the bytes, write as "sha256:" + 64 lowercase hex.
The profile_id in the mandate request names which profile; profile_hash names which bytes. Both parties MUST agree on both or refuse (PROFILE_HASH_MISMATCH).

A profile that declares the v0.8 fields (commitment_modes, maximum, requiredFor inside a per_transaction boundType, enforcedBy) hashes like any other: the hash covers the parsed document, whatever it declares.

canonical_prefix is not a value to reproduce: it is the first 80 characters of the canonical (JCS) serialization of the profile, given so that an implementation whose profile_hash differs can see where its bytes diverge.

cases.note: The published charge@0.5 profile. Re-indent the file, reorder its keys, or strip its trailing newline and the hash MUST NOT change.

Declares commitment_modes: ["review"] — a mandate under it may not be automatic (protocol.md → Commitment Modes, rule 8). Re-indent the file, reorder its keys, or strip its trailing newline and the hash MUST NOT change.

Declares maximum: 366 on read_max_age_days — the first bound with a profile-declared maximum (protocol.md → Bounds Schema, rule 9). Re-indent the file, reorder its keys, or strip its trailing newline and the hash MUST NOT change.

Declares requiredFor inside the per_transaction boundType of value_max and discount_max (protocol.md → Bounds Schema, rule 8). Re-indent the file, reorder its keys, or strip its trailing newline and the hash MUST NOT change.
